assumptions.assumption: Use no third-party dependencies. Record an ADR if the selected language departs from the default.
assumptions.why: Standard libraries suffice, keep the tool small, and avoid network-dependent installation.

assumptions.assumption: Support Windows, macOS, and Linux through the selected runtime or a locally compiled executable.
assumptions.why: The conversion needs no operating-system-specific features.

assumptions.assumption: Deliver source code with local run instructions; public package publishing and downloadable release binaries are outside the initial build.
assumptions.why: Local delivery fulfills the brief without requiring accounts, signing credentials, or publishing decisions.

assumptions.assumption: Accept C, Celsius, F, and Fahrenheit without case sensitivity, and ignore surrounding whitespace.
assumptions.why: These spellings are predictable and inexpensive to extend.

assumptions.assumption: Accept signed decimal and scientific-notation numbers, reject non-finite values, and impose no physical temperature limits.
assumptions.why: The requested operation is numeric conversion rather than physical validation.

assumptions.assumption: Print the converted number rounded to two decimal places, trim trailing fractional zeros, normalize negative zero, and append the destination unit and a newline.
assumptions.why: A compact output such as 212 F is readable; precision and formatting are inexpensive to adjust.

assumptions.assumption: Report missing input, invalid numbers, unsupported units, extra input, and non-finite conversion results on standard error with a nonzero exit status.
assumptions.why: Predictable failures make the tool usable from scripts without requiring a product decision.

assumptions.assumption: Provide built-in help and verify conversions using synthetic examples, including freezing points, boiling points, negative values, and invalid input.
assumptions.why: No human-supplied test data or external services are needed.
